page.layout: One printed page. At the top, the page number (27) and the heading "Alphabetum Samaritanum." Below it, an italic introductory paragraph. Then a table of letters in columns: number, Latin name, Samaritan letter, Hebrew letter, and on the right the numerals 80 to 1000 with their names and final forms. Beside the table on the right, a short text block. Below the table, a paragraph with a drop cap. At the foot, the catchword "Con-" at the right and the signature "E 2" at the left.

main_text.head: Alphabetum Samaritanum.
main_text.p: Habent Samaritani literas tantùm 22, Vt Hebræi; quarum ordo, potestas, & nomina, cum Hebræis eadem sunt, figurâ tantùm discrepant; nullas verò literarum initialium, finalium, vel mediarum discrepantes formas habent: ut ex Tabella sequenti liquet.
Reliquos numeros supplent ut apud Hebræos.
Puncta vocalia habent nulla, sed literæ [?] [?] [?] quæ matres lectionis apud Hebræos vocantur, eorum locum supplent, uti apud Syros, Arabes, Chaldæos, ante punctorum inventionem.

page.notes: The Samaritan letter forms, the Hebrew final forms and the inline matres lectionis glyphs are marked [?] because the scan is too small and faint to read them reliably. The inline glyphs after "literæ" appear to be Hebrew vav, yod and aleph. The drop cap P is joined to "uncta" as "Puncta"; the printed letter may be "Punćta". The table cells are reconstructed from the layout: the numerals 80 to 400 sit beside the first six letters, the text block "Reliquos numeros" sits beside rows 7 to 10, and the numerals 500 to 1000 sit beside rows 20 to 70. The printed "22" in the introduction is read as 22.
